title: The same formatter, on Linux, rewrites in place and passes through length zero — identically to darwin

provenance.evidence: Two readings. `src/main.rs` at inode 550240 goes 37 -> 0 bytes, then the SAME inode goes 0 -> 52 bytes. No temporary file appears at any reading; the inode never changes. Captured by tests/compatibility/save-patterns/v0/capture.mjs in the image built from Dockerfile.capture, against rustfmt 1.9.0-stable — the SAME build as the darwin capture, which is what makes the two comparable rather than merely similar.
blind_spots: open, flush, fsync and close are invisible to polling

objects.role: src/main.rs, the source file — one identity throughout

folder.fidelity: a backend that does not declare ObserveDurableBoundary
folder.omission_note: A formatter fast enough to finish inside one reading is seen as a single Written — the folder-watching backend's first declared restriction, and here the SAFE outcome, because the empty state is what gets skipped.

expected.meaningful_durable_change: src/main.rs holds the formatted text. One durable change for one formatter run over one file.
expected.forbidden_note: Mount sequence 2 and folder sequence 1 are the measured zero-length state, on Linux as on darwin.

notes: This is the CONTROL in the cross-platform pair. rustfmt produces byte-for-byte the same object-identity story on both platforms — one inode, through zero, back up — which is what licenses the corpus to treat in-place truncate-then-rewrite as a property of `File::create` + `write` rather than of a filesystem.

It matters that this one matches, because its neighbours do not: linux-vim-rename-over-with-backup and linux-git-checkout-in-place both diverge from their darwin counterparts. A corpus where every Linux capture diverged would suggest the capture method differs by platform; one where the formatter matches exactly and the editor does not locates the difference in the tools.
